claims.text: The axis is the net direction of ventricular depolarization in the frontal plane.
claims.quote: The "axis" refers to the net direction of ventricular depolarization in the frontal plane.

claims.text: Two-lead shortcut: look at lead I and aVF I positive, aVF positive: normal (−30° to +90°)
I positive, aVF negative: possible left axis deviation — check lead II
claims.quote: Positive Negative Possible Left Axis Deviation (check II)

claims.text: I negative, aVF positive: right axis deviation
I negative, aVF negative: extreme axis (“northwest”)
Lead I positive and aVF negative? If II is also positive the axis is still normal; if II is negative it is LAD
claims.quote: If Lead I is positive and aVF is negative, look at Lead II: if II is also positive, the axis is still normal; if II is negative, it's LAD.
